title: Lucid Air için UX 3.0 güncellemesi yayınlandı, eski modeller ücret gerektiriyor
summary: Lucid Motors, Air sedan modelleri için Gravity SUV'nin arayüzünü getiren UX 3.0 güncellemesini duyurdu. 2025 ve yeni modeller için ücretsiz olan güncelleme, bazı eski araçlar için 950 dolarlık işlemci değişimi gerektiriyor.
body:
Lucid Motors, Air sedan modelleri için Gravity SUV'nin arayüzünü temel alan yeni UX 3.0 güncellemesini duyurdu. İç eğlence ve kontrol sistemini daha hızlı ve sezgisel hale getirmeyi amaçlayan bu büyük yazılım paketi, InsideEVs ve Electrek gibi kaynakların aktardığına göre 29 Eylül 2025 ve sonrasındaki modeller için kablosuz olarak ücretsiz sunuluyor.

## Yeni arayüz neler sunuyor?

UX 3.0 güncellemesi, direksiyon arkasındaki kavisli ekran üzerinde kaydırılabilir kartlar sunarak müzik, şarj istasyonu kısayolları ve araç ayarlarına erişimi kolaylaştırıyor. Pilot Panel adı verilen dikey orta ekranda ise telefon benzeri aşağı kaydırılabilir hızlı kontroller yer alıyor. Güncelleme ayrıca harita rota planlamasını geliştiriyor, çoklu görev yeteneklerini artırıyor ve Apple CarPlay ile Android Auto entegrasyonlarını daha güvenilir hale getiriyor.

## Eski araçlar için işlemci değişimi

2022, 2023 ve 2024 model yılındaki bazı araçların ilk nesil işlemcileri yeni yazılımı çalıştırmak için yeterli donanım gücüne sahip değil. Bu durumdaki araç sahiplerinin, ABD'de montaj dahil 950 dolar ödeyerek bir bilgi-eğlence işlemcisi yükseltmesi yaptırması gerekiyor. Lucid yetkilileri diğer pazarlar için fiyat ve detayların yakında açıklanacağını belirtirken, donanım değişiminin gerekli olup olmadığını öğrenmek için müşterilerin müşteri hizmetleri ile iletişime geçmesi gerekiyor.

**Neden önemli?** Lucid Air sahipleri, markanın yeni Gravity SUV modelinde yer alan güncel dijital deneyimine kavuşurken, erken dönem araç sahiplerinin yeni arayüze geçmek için ek donanım ücreti ödemesi gerekecek.

source_texts.title: Lucid Rolled Out A Big Update For The Air. You Might Need New Hardware To Get It
source_texts.summary: Lucid is bringing a Gravity-like digital interface to the Air sedan. Older cars will need a $950 computer upgrade.
source_texts.text:
Lucid Rolled Out A Big Update For The Air. You Might Need New Hardware To Get It
Lucid is bringing a Gravity-like digital interface to the Air sedan. Older cars will need a $950 computer upgrade.
- Lucid's new user interface for the Air is here.
- It's supposed to make the infotainment system faster and more intuitive to use.
- For pre-2025 vehicles, UX 3.0 may require a $950 processor upgrade.
Lucid on Tuesday announced a redesigned user interface for the Air intended to make the experience faster and more intuitive. The UX 3.0 update brings a new route planning feature, updated Apple CarPlay and Android Auto integrations, and improved multitasking, among other upgrades. But if you have an older Air, getting the new system won't be as simple as downloading some new software.
The new digital experience, which helps bring the Air up to par with the system that debuted in the Gravity SUV, is available as an over-the-air update for 2025-and-newer Air models. It'll arrive automatically through Lucid's 2.11.0 software update.
For 2022, 2023, and some 2024 models, UX 3.0 will be available with a $950 processor upgrade. That's the price in the U.S., including installation, and Lucid says it will share details for other markets soon. The hardware retrofit is only necessary for some 2024 models, a Lucid spokesperson said, because the switchover to the second-generation infotainment processor happened midway through that model year.
The new system features swipeable cards on the left side of the sweeping "Cockpit Panel" that display frequently used features. It also includes new "Quick Controls," which let drivers swipe down from the top of the lower vertically-oriented "Pilot Panel" to access popular settings. It updates the route planning feature to include preferences for charging networks, arrival range, and charging adapter capability.
The new software allows drivers to "move more smoothly among navigation, media, vehicle controls, and apps across the Cockpit and Pilot Panel displays," Lucid says. It now lets drivers put their navigation up on the upper screen and fiddle with the music on the lower "Pilot Panel," a feature that always felt like it was missing from the Air.
Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, Lucid says, should be more reliable now and appear larger on the Air's crescent-shaped screen.

source_texts.text:
Lucid Air owners are finally getting the Gravity’s interface. Lucid started pushing Air UX 3.0 today as part of software version 2.11.0, its biggest Air software overhaul in years.
Owners of 2025 and newer Airs get it for free over the air. But if you bought a 2022, 2023, or some 2024 Air, you’ll first need a $950 infotainment processor upgrade at a Lucid service center.
What’s new in Air UX 3.0
Lucid says the new software is modeled on the Gravity SUV’s interface, which picked up a Gold iF Design Award in 2024. The company is promising faster, more responsive screens and less digging through menus.
The biggest change is on the curved Cockpit Panel behind the steering wheel. Its Home screen is now a stack of swipeable cards: your music, a shortcut to charging stops nearby, one-tap routing home or to work, calls, and car settings. Pull a card down and the full app opens on the Pilot Panel, the vertical touchscreen in the center console.
The Pilot Panel gets a new Quick Controls menu you pull down from the top of the screen, much like a phone. Lucid also claims apps now hand off between the two displays with less lag.
Here’s the rest of what’s in the update:
- Navigation: a revamped dual-screen layout, Favorites, and Auto Dark Mode
- EV routing: pick preferred charging networks, include stations that work with Lucid-approved adapters, and set a minimum arrival range
- Profiles: faster switching, more control for the Primary profile over linked keys, an easier Guest reset, and a six-digit PIN to exit Guest mode
- Apple CarPlay and Android Auto: both now stretch across the full right side of the Cockpit display, over wireless or USB
That last one matters more than it sounds. Lucid only added CarPlay as standard across its lineup in 2023, and a lot of owners live in it. Giving the phone projection more screen and, according to Lucid, better reliability is a direct response to how people actually use the car.
Marc Solsona Palomar, Lucid’s VP of Software, said Air owners “will enjoy more reliable and intuitive experiences” with the update.
The $950 catch for early Air owners
Early Airs don’t have the processing power to run the new interface. Lucid is offering an infotainment processor swap for $950 in the US, installation included but taxes extra. Pricing in other markets hasn’t been announced, and owners have to contact Lucid Customer Care to check eligibility.
So the people who took a chance on Lucid first, some of whom paid $169,000 for a 2022 Air Dream Edition, are the ones being asked to pay again.
Lucid isn’t the first to do this. Tesla launched an infotainment computer retrofit for older Model S and Model X vehicles at $2,500 in 2020, then cut it to $1,500 amid controversy. Lucid’s price is lower, but it applies to cars that are only two to four years old, not eight.
This is only the third major version of the Air’s interface since deliveries started in late 2021. Lucid pushed UX 2.0 to the Air in October 2022, about a year after first deliveries.
Electrek’s Take
This update is much needed. Lucid’s hardware is excellent. Its software isn’t there yet.
When we reviewed the Lucid Gravity GT earlier this year, we were stunned by how good it is. It drives like a dream, it’s incredibly efficient for its size, and the range is class-leading. We gave it 86.3 out of 100, and it would’ve scored much higher if not for the software. The seat app froze and needed a reset. Navigation opened and closed on its own. We asked for seat ventilation and got the seat heater. The car lost track of the key after short absences. The whole system felt like the CPU was pegged at 100% by background processes.
That’s the same interface Lucid is now porting to the Air. So the redesign is only half the job. Lucid already had to publicly promise to fix Gravity software problems last December after a wave of owner complaints, and the bugs we hit this summer show it’s not done.
If Lucid gets the software to the level of its hardware, it’s a top-tier EV maker. Its motors, efficiency, and packaging are already ahead of almost everyone. Software is what keeps people cross-shopping a Tesla or a Rivian.
As for the $950, we think Lucid should eat that cost for early adopters, or at least discount it heavily. Those owners funded the company when it needed it most and put up with the roughest software along the way. Will Lucid treat them like it wants to keep them?
